episodes.title: Build the identity foundation
episodes.subtitle: DC01 + DC02 / Active Directory & DNS
episodes.description: Configure Active Directory and DNS on Windows Server 2025, understand why two controllers matter, and keep a record of the build.

chapters.label: Plan the build
chapters.title: Give every system a purpose
chapters.description: Understand AD and DNS before choosing names, addresses, and the starting configuration.
chapters.network: DC01 and DC02 are planned. The connections show where identity services will take shape.

chapters.label: Configure DC01
chapters.title: Create the first service point
chapters.description: Create the forest and bring Active Directory Domain Services and DNS online on DC01.
chapters.network: DC01 is configured. DC02 remains a planned system until it joins this same domain.

chapters.label: Bring in DC02
chapters.title: Give the domain a second home
chapters.description: Add a second writable controller and understand the availability it provides.
chapters.network: Both controllers serve the domain. The moving connection follows directory replication.

chapters.label: Verify DNS
chapters.title: Follow the discovery path
chapters.description: Query each DNS server and compare the returned service records and addresses with your plan.
chapters.network: Select either controller below to trace a DNS query from the client through the switch.

chapters.label: Keep evidence
chapters.title: Leave a build you can explain
chapters.description: Record the configuration, observed results, and follow-up work in your training companion.
chapters.network: Identity and DNS now have two service points. Your build record connects choices with evidence.

courses.title: Risk Management Framework
courses.subtitle: Scope, categorization, and control selection
courses.description: Apply the Risk Management Framework (RMF) to the system built in Inside the Network. Establish responsibilities and boundaries, justify mission impacts, and select a defensible control set before developing its Body of Evidence.
outcomes: Explain the RMF lifecycle and authorization responsibilities.
Define and categorize the Inside the Network practice system.
Select and tailor controls with documented ownership and rationale.

stages.title: RMF and authorization fundamentals
stages.detail: Explain the relationship between the RMF lifecycle, the Body of Evidence, the authorization package, and the authorization decision.

stages.title: Prepare and define the system
stages.detail: Establish what is being authorized, why it exists, and which organizational and system preparation decisions must be made before documentation expands.

stages.title: Categorize information and impacts
stages.detail: Justify confidentiality, integrity, and availability impacts using information types and mission consequences. Treat privacy applicability as an explicit decision.

stages.title: Select and tailor controls
stages.detail: Translate the approved categorization and applicable requirements into a justified, assignable control set. Distinguish the control catalog from a selected baseline.

courses.title: Body of Evidence
courses.subtitle: Document, demonstrate, and assess the network
courses.description: Develop the Body of Evidence for the same Inside the Network build. Write the System Security Plan, connect implementation to proof, organize evidence, and assess findings and residual risk for authorization review.
outcomes: Write specific implementation statements for the practice system.
Organize traceable, current technical and operational evidence.
Assess selected objectives and document findings, risk, and corrective actions.

stages.title: Write the system security plan
stages.detail: Write a System Security Plan (SSP) that describes the actual system and explains how selected controls are implemented.

stages.title: Connect implementation to proof
stages.detail: Collect technical and operational evidence that addresses the selected requirement and can support an assessment.

stages.title: Organize the Body of Evidence
stages.detail: Make evidence easy to retrieve, trace, and maintain across system changes and assessment cycles.

stages.title: Plan and perform assessment
stages.detail: Turn implementation claims into assessable objectives and distinguish a planned test from an observed result.

stages.title: Manage findings and residual risk
stages.detail: Translate weaknesses into mission-relevant risk and an accountable response. Explain the difference between technical severity and contextual risk.

relatedResources.title: Open the Body of Evidence workspace
relatedResources.detail: Ten examples with editable Markdown and CSV starters

courses.title: Authorization to Operate
courses.subtitle: Assemble, brief, and maintain the authorization package
courses.description: Turn the network’s Body of Evidence into a reviewable Authorization to Operate (ATO) package. Assemble the submission, brief the Authorizing Official on supported conclusions and remaining risk, and maintain evidence after the decision. Complete the shared course with the package capstone.
outcomes: Assemble a consistent authorization package for the practice system.
Present supported conclusions and residual risk for the Authorizing Official’s decision.
Complete the package capstone and plan ongoing monitoring.

stages.title: Assemble the authorization package
stages.detail: Build a reviewable package whose claims, assessment results, and open risks agree across documents.

stages.title: Present the authorization decision
stages.detail: Communicate mission need, the assessed security posture, unresolved risk, and proposed risk responses to the decision maker.

stages.title: Monitor and maintain authorization
stages.detail: Keep the authorization evidence useful as the system, threats, personnel, and dependencies change.

relatedResources.title: Open the authorization package capstone
relatedResources.detail: Four hour exercise · Assemble, defend, and maintain the practice package

relatedResources.title: Open the package manifest
relatedResources.detail: Organize the evidence and submission records

stages.title: Map names to the network
stages.detail: A DNS plan explains which server owns a name and how a client finds that server. Begin with the working directory build, then extend it deliberately.

stages.title: Configure forward and reverse zones
stages.detail: Forward lookup answers where a name lives. Reverse lookup answers which name is assigned to an address. AD integration lets the directory replicate zone data between the selected DNS servers.

stages.title: Create and maintain service records
stages.detail: Build a small, intentional record set. A host record identifies a machine; an alias provides a stable service name without making that alias a separate server.

stages.title: Prove resolution and directory discovery
stages.detail: Test each server explicitly before testing client fallback. A successful cached answer does not prove that both DNS servers hold the right records.

stages.title: Find the fault and record the fix
stages.detail: Troubleshoot one layer at a time: client settings, server reachability, authoritative data, replication, and finally the application that uses the name.

courses.title: Configure DNS
courses.subtitle: Zones, records, replication & troubleshooting
courses.description: Build dependable internal name resolution on DC01 and DC02. Configure forward and reverse zones, manage service records, and prove DNS redundancy in the air-gapped training network.
outcomes: Plan authoritative internal DNS and client settings.
Configure secure AD-integrated zones and maintain records.
Test both resolvers, directory discovery, and client fallback.

stages.title: Design the two-tier trust hierarchy
stages.detail: The root establishes trust. The subordinate, also called the issuing CA in this design, handles approved end-entity certificates. Keeping these roles separate protects the root from daily network exposure.

stages.title: Configure the offline Root CA
stages.detail: Treat root installation as a controlled event. Its private key is the highest-value secret in the hierarchy, and its configuration shapes the subordinate certificate it will sign.

stages.title: Create the issuing CA request
stages.detail: Prepare the online issuing server, but keep issuance paused until its CA certificate has been signed and installed. The request carries the public key; the private key stays protected on the issuing system or its approved key provider.

stages.title: Sign through the offline ceremony
stages.detail: A signing ceremony connects an approved request to an approved CA identity. A matching filename alone is not proof that the root should trust the request.

stages.title: Activate issuance and publish trust data
stages.detail: A running CA is only one part of a working PKI. Clients also need the approved trust anchor, the intermediate certificate, and current revocation information at the advertised locations.

stages.title: Validate enrollment, revocation, and recovery
stages.detail: Finish from a clean domain client. Verify the experience of a relying system, including what happens when a certificate is no longer trusted.

courses.title: Configure a Root CA & issuing CA
courses.subtitle: Offline root + subordinate CA / Two-tier PKI
courses.description: Build a two-tier public key infrastructure with an offline standalone Root CA and an enterprise subordinate/issuing CA. Follow the signing ceremony, publish trust and revocation data, and validate enrollment.
outcomes: Design the CA hierarchy and its publication dependencies.
Configure the offline root and sign an issuing CA request through controlled media transfer.
Publish trust data and prove certificate enrollment and revocation.

stages.title: Design and build the OU structure
stages.detail: Organizational units exist for delegation and Group Policy targeting, not to mirror an org chart. Build the structure the hardening policies will hang on before importing any of them.

stages.title: Stage the tooling across the air gap
stages.detail: The hardening content is downloaded artifacts: the DISA GPO package, the SCAP Compliance Checker (SCC), and STIG Viewer. They cross the boundary the way everything does here — reviewed, hashed, and carried on approved removable media.

stages.title: Capture the pre-hardening baseline
stages.detail: Measure before you change. A scan of the freshly built controllers shows the honest starting point, teaches what the operating system already secures by default, and becomes the before picture every later scan is compared against.

stages.title: Import and link the DISA GPOs
stages.detail: Group Policy is how the STIG becomes configuration. Import the package into the central store, link by organizational unit, and keep the lab's deliberate deviations written down rather than silently skipped.

stages.title: Rescan, reconcile, and record
stages.detail: The second scan is the verdict. Compare it with the baseline, let the automated results fill the checklists, and give every remaining open item a human answer.

stages.title: Set the rescan cadence and exception record
stages.detail: Hardening is a state you maintain, not a step you finish. Close the course by deciding who rescans, when, and which event forces an early look.

courses.title: Harden the baseline
courses.subtitle: OU design, DISA GPOs & STIG/SCAP verification
courses.description: Design the organizational unit structure, apply the DISA STIG Group Policy package to the verified network core, and prove the result with before-and-after SCAP scans, reconciled checklists, and a documented exception record.
outcomes: Design OUs for delegation and policy targeting, and redirect the default containers.
Import the DISA GPO package and link STIG policies by organizational unit.
Verify hardening with baseline and rescan SCAP results, reconciled checklists, and documented exceptions.
